thread:
Mike: Hey folks, seeing a weird pattern in eu-west1 this morning — lots of tiny GPU pods in Pending while a few nodes are 90% reserved. Latency for small inference jobs jumped ~2.3x. Anyone else? :eyes:
Ashley: Yup saw alerts. Grafana shows a ton of 1-GPU pod churn and many nodes with fragmented free slots. Link: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west1/gpu-allocs
Sara: This smells like reserved capacity + zone skew. Dedicated pools holding whole cards for customers, but scheduler can't pack tiny pods => fragmentation. Cost team flagged higher unit cost too.
Mike: Exactly. Logs from scheduler show repeated attach/detach and soft-evict loops. Snippet: ```I0312 09:12:02 scheduler.go:212] failed to pack pod: insufficient contiguous gpus on node-27
I0312 09:12:02 attach-detach-controller: attach timeout, retry
```
Jules: Any recent rollout on taint/affinity heuristics? We pushed the affinity priority tweak yesterday night.
Ashley: We did change preferSameRack -> preferSameAZ weighting from 25->10. Could be letting pods scatter more. Rollout notes: https://deploys.redwood/edge/affinity-weight-2026-03-12
DevOpsBot: @channel Autoscaler temporarily disabled warm-pools in eu-west1 at 09:30 for a config revert.
Sara: That would reduce warm node availability and make fragmentation worse. Can we re-enable warm pools but restrict to nodes without Dedicated reservations?
Mike: Proposed short-term mitigation: 1) squash affinity weight back to 25 2) enable a compacting descheduler job to coalesce tiny pods 3) surgically drain a small batch of reserved nodes for reprovisioning (non-production first). Thoughts?
Jules: +1 for descheduler. We can run a targeted job with policy: remove-below-utilization=30% age>10m label:k8s.io/scheduler-allow=compact. Should avoid mass evictions.
Ashley: Also add a patch to scheduler to prefer packing by fractional-gpu hint label (workload hint) — low-risk config change.
Sara: Ops note: customers on Dedicated will notice if we throttle their reserved pools. Need CS heads-in-loop before draining. I'll loop in @CustomerOps.
Mike: Good call. Action items: Ashley to revert affinity weight (hotfix), Jules to run descheduler canary in eu-west1 (limit 5 nodes), Sara to coordinate CS/Legal for any reserved node touch. I'll monitor queues and post metrics in 15m.
Ashley: Revert done (rolled back to 25) — deploy id: rollback-425.
Jules: Kicking descheduler canary now (job: compact-canary-eu1, 5 nodes). Will post results.
DevOpsBot: descheduler job started compact-canary-eu1 at 09:46, target nodes: node-21,node-24,node-27,node-33,node-38
Mike: Awesome. If latency drops, we schedule gradual descheduler run and follow with scheduler packing policy tweak.
Sara: Filed a customer advisory draft for CS: "We may perform limited maintenance to rebalance reserved capacity in eu-west1 to improve latency for shared workloads." Tagging CS for approval.
Ashley: FYI I also added a metric: fragmentation_index per-az to Grafana. Dashboards updated.
Jules: Canary finished: reclaimed 6 fragmented slots, average small-pod pending dropped from 42 -> 8 on the canary nodes. No errors.
Mike: Nice. Leave canary running for 2h, then plan rolling run with 2% velocity. Keep reactions on slack and I'll update infra runbook. :thumbsup:
Sara: I'll schedule the CS notification after we confirm 1h stable.
Mike: Thanks all. If anything regresses, we revert descheduler and affinity revert.
